title: Revit Worksharing and Collaboration Practice
purpose: Implement governed S6 collaboration and workset principles in Revit authoring models through bounded worksharing, ownership, workset, maintenance, and recovery practices.
preconditions: The project collaboration environment and authoritative model locations are governed under S3 and S6.
The project workset strategy is defined and aligned with the governed S4 naming structure.
Project-specific cloud or central/local mechanics are confirmed before applying source-era local-file guidance.

steps.name: Use governed multi-user authoring pattern
actions: Open and edit the governed authoring model through the project-approved multi-user Revit workflow.
Do not directly edit a protected central/source model where the deployment pattern requires local or cloud-mediated authoring.
Synchronize or publish changes at the project-defined cadence and before ending the work session.
validation: The user session follows the approved project worksharing pattern.
Changes are synchronized or published through the governed collaboration path.
failure_modes: Direct editing bypasses the governed collaboration pattern.
A stale local or unstable session is propagated into shared production.

steps.name: Apply worksets as containment and ownership structure
actions: Use worksets for governed containment, ownership boundaries, and high-level visibility rather than fine-grained graphics styling.
Place datum/reference content only on the governed datum workset or equivalent project-defined structure.
Place linked models on governed link worksets.
Keep temporary or troubleshooting worksets controlled and remove or close them when no longer needed.
Do not create personal user-named worksets.
validation: Workset assignment follows the project-governed S4 workset grammar and S6 containment intent.
Modeled geometry is not placed on the datum/reference workset.
Links reside on governed link worksets.
failure_modes: Worksets are used as an ad-hoc graphics system.
Personal or uncontrolled worksets appear in production.
Physical geometry is placed on a datum/reference workset.

steps.name: Borrow minimally and release ownership
actions: Borrow only elements required for the active task.
Coordinate before editing another user's active scope.
Release ownership through regular synchronization and avoid checking out large portions of the model without explicit coordination.
validation: Element ownership remains bounded to active work.
Persistent ownership conflicts are escalated rather than ignored.
failure_modes: Large scopes remain checked out without need.
Repeated ownership or synchronization warnings are ignored.

steps.name: Maintain model health and controlled upgrades
actions: Perform project-governed model maintenance such as cleanup, audit, or compact at the approved cadence.
Back up and archive a known-good model state before a governed Revit-version upgrade.
Validate the upgraded model with project-defined smoke checks before production resumes.
validation: Maintenance and upgrade actions are traceable.
A rollback-capable pre-upgrade state exists when an upgrade is performed.
failure_modes: Upgrade occurs without governance or rollback preparation.
Known model-health errors are propagated into production.

steps.name: Stop propagation when corruption or instability is suspected
actions: Stop synchronization when corruption, repeated errors, or an unstable local/session is suspected.
Notify the project BIM support/coordination authority.
Recover from a fresh governed source or last known good backup using the project-approved recovery path.
validation: Unstable sessions are isolated from shared production.
Recovery uses a traceable governed source.
failure_modes: An unstable local/session is synchronized into the governed model.

outputs: Workshared Revit model following governed S6 collaboration practice
Controlled workset assignment and ownership state
Traceable maintenance, upgrade, or recovery actions where applicable
evidence: Workset inventory and element assignment report
governance_notes: S6 remains the normative authority for collaboration, linking, and shared-coordinate requirements; this object only implements those rules in Revit.
Source-era central/local mechanics are conditional implementation guidance because current project collaboration may use cloud worksharing rather than file-based locals.
Source workset names were examples; governed workset syntax comes from the S4 naming structure.

provenance.migration_note: Mixed normative/instruction source normalized to L6 under existing S6/S4 authority. Placeholder workset names and unresolved role/RACI statements were not promoted.
